name: Catherine Blakespear
title: California State Senator, Chair of the Senate Environmental Quality Committee
district: California State Senate District 38 (northern San Diego County and southern Orange County, coastal)
background: Blakespear describes herself as a fourth-generation San Diegan. She earned a B.S./M.S. in journalism from Northwestern University in 1999 and a J.D. from the University of Utah's S.J. Quinney College of Law in 2006. She worked as a journalist for the Los Angeles Times and the Associated Press before practicing law at Ray Quinney & Nebeker. (Source: official Senate biography, sd38.senate.ca.gov, and Ballotpedia, Catherine Blakespear.)

She entered local government as a traffic commissioner and city council member in Encinitas before being elected Mayor of Encinitas in 2016. She was elected to the State Senate in November 2022 for the open, newly drawn District 38 seat, defeating Republican Matt Gunderson 52.2% to 47.8% after both advanced from a nonpartisan top-two primary. She was re-elected in the June 2026 primary with 51.9% against Republican Laura Bassett, advancing to the November 2026 general election. (Source: Ballotpedia, Catherine Blakespear.)

In the Senate she chairs the Environmental Quality Committee (2025 to 2026 session) and previously chaired the Human Services Committee (2023 to 2024 session). Her official biography describes her focus areas as economic opportunity, environmental protection, public safety, homelessness reduction, and transportation. (Source: official Senate biography.)

voting_record_highlights: SB 417 (2023), regulating licensed firearms dealers: Blakespear was lead author. The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 32 to 5 on September 6, 2023 (Assembly floor vote 63 to 0), and Gov. Gavin Newsom signed it September 26, 2023 as Chapter 252, Statutes of 2023. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status and vote record for SB 417.)

SB 452 (2023), a firearms-regulation bill Blakespear authored: the Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 30 to 9 on September 14, 2023 (Assembly floor vote 55 to 18), and Gov. Newsom signed it September 26, 2023 as Chapter 253, Statutes of 2023. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status and vote record for SB 452.)

SB 7 (2024), addressing regional housing-need determinations: Blakespear was lead author. The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 31 to 8 on August 28, 2024 (Assembly floor vote 54 to 16), and Gov. Newsom signed it September 19, 2024 as Chapter 283, Statutes of 2024. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status and vote record for SB 7.)

SB 954 (2026), a CEQA exemption for advanced manufacturing facilities Blakespear authored: it passed both houses (Assembly amendments concurred in 28 to 10 on August 28, 2026) but was vetoed by Gov. Newsom on September 18, 2026, matching a press statement on her official Senate site responding to the veto. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 954; sd38.senate.ca.gov newsroom.)

SB 42 (2025 to 2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026: Blakespear was a Senate Principal Coauthor (the three lead authors were Umberg, Allen, and Cervantes). The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 29 to 8 on September 13, 2025, and Gov. Newsom signed it October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025, placing the measure before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot. Full detail on the measure itself is covered in content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json and is not duplicated here.
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Senator Blakespear was found. Direct inspection of leginfo.legislature.ca.gov's vote-history pages for several of her bills (SB 417, SB 452, SB 7, SB 954) confirms the Legislature publishes only bill-by-bill roll-call votes (ayes, noes, and members not voting per motion), not an aggregated per-member attendance record. There is no senate.ca.gov or leginfo.legislature.ca.gov page reporting an overall attendance rate for any senator.
